questions.statement: When I was a child, I ________ play with dolls every afternoon.

options.feedback: Correct! We use "used to" for past habits that don't happen now.
Incorrect. This means being familiar with something now.

questions.explanation:
"Used to" se utiliza para describir hábitos o estados que eran frecuentes en el pasado pero que ya no ocurren en el presente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I ________ like broccoli when I was little, but now I love it!

options.feedback: Correct! In negatives with "didn't", we remove the "-d" from "use".
Incorrect. You cannot have two past markers (did + used).

questions.explanation:
Para oraciones negativas, usamos el auxiliar "didn't" seguido de "use to" (sin la -d final).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ you ________ have long hair when you were at primary school?

options.feedback: Correct! Question structure: Did + subject + use to.

questions.explanation:
Al igual que en las negativas, en las preguntas usamos el auxiliar "Did" y por lo tanto el verbo "use" pierde la -d.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: There ________ be a park here, but now there is a shopping mall.

options.feedback: Correct! "Used to" can describe past states or existence of things.

questions.explanation:
"Used to" no solo sirve para acciones repetidas, sino también para estados pasados (como el hecho de que algo existiera en un lugar).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He ________ smoke a lot, but he quit two years ago.

options.feedback: Correct! It was a past habit that ended.

questions.explanation:
Este es el uso más común: contrastar algo que hacíamos frecuentemente con el hecho de que ya no lo hacemos.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Before the Transmilenio was built in Bogotá, people ________ travel in smaller buses called "busetas".

options.feedback: Correct! Describing a historical habit or common situation.

questions.explanation:
"Used to" es muy útil para hablar de cómo ha cambiado la vida en una ciudad o país a lo largo de los años.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: In which case can we NOT use "would" as a substitute for "used to"?

options.text: When I lived in the country, I used to walk to school.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Walking is an action, so "would walk" is possible.

options.text: I used to be very shy when I was a teenager.
options.feedback: Correct! "Would" cannot be used for past states (like "be" or "have").

options.text: We used to visit my grandparents every Sunday.
I used to eat a lot of candy.

questions.explanation:
Aunque "would" puede describir hábitos pasados, solo funciona con verbos de acción. Para verbos de estado (be, have, live, believe), solo podemos usar "used to".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"My city **used to be** very quiet."
What does this imply about the city now?

options.text: It is probably noisy or busy now.
options.feedback: Correct! "Used to" implies that the situation has changed.

options.text: It will be quiet in the future.

questions.explanation:
La carga pragmática de "used to" es el cambio. Si algo "solía ser" de una forma, es porque ahora es de otra.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I ________ early mornings because I have been a baker for ten years.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would mean you no longer wake up early.
Correct! "Be used to + -ing/noun" means to be familiar with or accustomed to something.
Incorrect. This means the process of becoming accustomed.

questions.explanation:
Un nivel B1 avanzado requiere distinguir "Used to" (hábito pasado) de "Be used to" (estar acostumbrado a algo en el presente).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"I **didn't used to (A)** like **living (B)** in the city, but I **got used to (C)** the noise **eventually (D)**."
questions.context: Identifying grammatical errors in complex sentences.

options.feedback: Correct! Error found. After "didn't", it must be "use to" (without the -d).
Incorrect. Correct use for the process of becoming accustomed.

questions.explanation:
El error más común con "used to" es olvidar quitar la -d en las formas negativa e interrogativa.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best expresses nostalgia for the past?

options.text: I remember how we used to spend hours talking under that old tree.
options.feedback: Correct! "Used to" combined with "remember" creates a nostalgic tone.

options.text: I am used to talking to my friends.
I will use to talk to you.

questions.explanation:
El uso de "used to" es fundamental para la expresión de emociones ligadas al pasado, como la nostalgia o la reflexión sobre el cambio personal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"Before the internet, children used to spend most of their time playing outside. Nowadays, they are used to having a screen in their hands from a very young age."
What is the main point?
questions.context: Selecting the best summary of a life change.

options.text: There has been a significant shift from outdoor activities to digital habits in childhood.
options.feedback: Correct! It captures the contrast between the past habit and the current familiar state.

options.text: Children always played with computers in the past.
Playing outside is the same as playing with screens.

questions.explanation: Parafrasear cambios sociales requiere entender la diferencia entre lo que "solía ser" (used to) y lo que ahora es "normal" o "familiar" (be used to).
